lines: Riley Chen
+1 (555) 010-7731 | riley.chen@example.com | example.com/in/riley-chen
EDUCATION
Northfield School of Management | MBA | Metro City, USA | Sep 2023 - Jun 2025
Lakeview University | B.A. in Economics | Lake City, USA | Sep 2014 - Jun 2018
EXPERIENCE
Coastal Marine Services | Diesel Mechanic | Lake City, USA | Jul 2025 - Present
- Rebuilt diesel engines and gearboxes for a fleet of 14 commercial fishing vessels, keeping dry-dock time under 5 days per job.
- Maintained hydraulic winch systems and logged service records for the harbor authority's annual inspections.
Crestline Logistics | Operations Analyst | Lake City, USA | Jul 2018 - Aug 2023
- Rebuilt weekly carrier scorecards used by 6 regional managers to renegotiate contracts, cutting late deliveries from 11% to 7% in two quarters.
- Cut warehouse pick errors 30% at two sites; my redesign of the slotting rules was rolled out with the floor supervisors and 45 retrained pickers.
- Ran the quarterly S&OP review across sales, finance and operations for 12 consecutive quarters, introducing a consensus forecast that cut forecast error from 18% to 11%.

- Led the rollout of a route-planning tool to 3 depots while rewriting the standard operating procedures, running driver training and taking over vendor negotiations for the telematics contract, which saved 1,800 driver hours a year across the region.
Harbor Payments | Associate Product Manager Intern | Metro City, USA | Jun 2024 - Aug 2024
- Redesigned merchant onboarding around a single verification step, cutting median time to first payment from 9 days to 4 across 2,300 new merchants in the pilot region.
- Lifted checkout conversion from 61% to 66% by testing a one-page flow against the three-step flow across 40,000 sessions, then shipping it to all merchants.
- Prioritized the dispute roadmap with RICE, scoring Reach as the number of support tickets each feature would close.
- After interviewing 25 merchants, mapping chargeback reasons, sizing the loss by segment and drafting a business case with finance, set the next quarter's roadmap priority.
- Ran the checkout A/B test with randomization by session and reported the 5-point conversion lift as the effect on merchants' customers.
- Presented the onboarding results and a follow-up roadmap to the payments leadership team, who funded the rollout to two more regions.
PROJECTS
Campus Food Rescue App | Product Lead | Student Venture | Oct 2023 - Present
- Launched a surplus-food pickup app to 3,100 students with two dining halls, redistributing 9 tonnes of food that would have been thrown away in its first year.
- Raised weekly active users from 400 to 1,150, a 150% increase, by adding pickup reminders chosen after 60 user interviews.
- Raised the pickup-slot fill rate by 20% across two dining halls, from 75% to 95%, by setting up a volunteer shift system.
MBA Consulting Practicum | Team Lead | Regional Hospital Network | Jan 2024 - May 2024
- Sized a $2.4M annual saving from consolidating outpatient scheduling across 4 clinics; the client funded a pilot based on the model.
- Patient intake at 4 clinics was mapped and the intake form was shortened, with the changes adopted by front-desk staff.
- Presented the final recommendation to the hospital COO and clinic directors, who approved a 90-day scheduling pilot at two clinics.
SKILLS
Product: roadmapping, A/B testing, user interviews, requirements writing
Tools: Jira, Amplitude, Excel

items.says: Keep the LinkedIn link only if the profile is current and supports the résumé.
items.because: A stale profile can weaken a strong application.

items.says: Move the Harbor Payments internship above Crestline Logistics.
items.because: The current order moves from 2025 back to 2018 and then forward to 2024, making the most relevant product experience easy to miss.

items.says: Specify the period covered by the engine and gearbox work.
items.because: It would make the scale easier to assess.

items.says: Clarify whether the under-five-day dry-dock time was your result or a team standard.
items.because: It would make your contribution easier to assess.

items.says: Add a substantiated result of the maintenance and records work.
items.because: As written, the bullet describes duties rather than impact.

items.says: Clarify your role in the contract renegotiations and delivery improvement.
items.because: The bullet connects the scorecards to both without distinguishing what you owned.

items.says: Make your ownership of the slotting change and implementation easier to follow.
items.because: The second half contains several actors.

items.says: Clarify what you changed about the forecasting process.
items.because: The forecast-error improvement should connect to a specific decision you drove.

items.says: Split or narrow the route-planning bullet if space permits.
items.because: Tool rollout, procedures, training, vendor negotiations, and time savings compete for attention.

items.says: Identify which actions produced the 1,800-hour saving.
Clarify whether the 2,300 merchants were in the measured pilot.
Clarify what you personally owned in the onboarding redesign.
Describe the conversion change as 5 percentage points, not 5%.
Check that “all merchants” accurately describes the rollout.
Revisit the Reach measure and explain why it was appropriate or use the measure actually used.
items.because: Support tickets closed may be an impact or workload proxy rather than the number of customers affected.

items.says: Combine or distinguish this from the preceding roadmap bullet.
items.because: Both cover roadmap prioritization.

items.says: State the roadmap decision or outcome more precisely.
items.because: The activity list currently obscures it.

items.says: The separate A/B-test bullet repeats the checkout bullet.
Session-level randomization does not necessarily support a lasting effect on merchants’ customers.
items.because: It supports a claim about sessions.

items.says: Clarify your contribution to securing approval for the two-region rollout.
items.because: The bullet relies on the presentation alone.

items.says: Identify the basis for “would have been thrown away” if it is an estimate.
items.because: Otherwise it reads as a counterfactual you may not be able to verify.

items.says: The increase from 400 to 1,150 is 187.5%, not 150%.
Distinguish whether reminders caused the user increase or were one contributing change.
The increase from 75% to 95% is 20 percentage points, not a 20% relative increase.
Clarify how the volunteer system connects to the fill-rate result.
Make clear that $2.4M was projected annual savings, not realized savings.
Identify your contribution to the patient-intake changes.
items.because: The passive construction hides your role.

items.says: Add an observable result of the patient-intake changes.
Clarify the link between shortening the intake form and the scheduling recommendation.
items.because: The link is currently unclear.

items.says: Consider consolidating this with the first practicum bullet.
items.because: Both describe the recommendation leading to an approved pilot.

items.says: Make sure the A/B-testing skill matches the level of analysis you performed.
items.because: Skills should be demonstrable in the bullets.

items.says: Add relevant tools if you used them hands-on and can discuss them.
items.because: The current list is short.

items.says: Confirm that “Present” still applies to the student venture.
items.because: The MBA graduation date is June 2025.
